source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: 1 Kings 1: all 53 public verses bind one-to-one to matching Hebrew records.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Preserves the doubled aging description and bodily weakness without an unstated diagnosis.
verses.before: King David was old, advanced in days. They covered him with garments, but he could not get warm.
verses.after: King David was old, advanced in years. They covered him with blankets, but he could not get warm.
verses.tsw_comparator: King David was old, advanced in days. They covered him with garments, but he could not get warm.

verses.rationale: Keeps her proposed care and bodily proximity without turning the plan into a stated marriage.
verses.before: So his servants said to him, “Let them seek for my lord the king a young virgin, that she may attend the king and care for him. Let her lie in your arms, and my lord the king will become warm.”
verses.after: His servants said to him, “Let a young virgin be found for my lord the king. She can attend the king and care for him. Let her lie in your arms, so my lord the king may grow warm.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So his servants said to him, “Let them seek for my lord the king a young virgin, that she may attend the king and care for him. Let her lie in your arms, and my lord the king will become warm.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the search criterion, full territory, and her identity.
verses.before: So they searched throughout all the territory of Israel for a beautiful young woman, and they found Abishag the Shunammite and brought her to the king.
verses.after: They searched throughout Israel’s territory for a beautiful young woman. They found Abishag the Shunammite and brought her to the king.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they searched throughout all the territory of Israel for a beautiful young woman, and they found Abishag the Shunammite and brought her to the king.

verses.rationale: Makes the knowing idiom explicit while retaining the narrator’s distinction between care and intercourse.
verses.before: The young woman was exceedingly beautiful. She cared for the king and served him, but the king did not know her.
verses.after: The young woman was very beautiful. She cared for the king and attended him, but the king did not have sexual relations with her.
verses.tsw_comparator: The young woman was exceedingly beautiful. She cared for the king and served him, but the king did not know her.

verses.rationale: Keeps self-exaltation and the display that echoes Absalom, with horsemen as stated here.
verses.before: Now Adonijah son of Haggith exalted himself, saying, “I will be king.” He prepared for himself chariots and horsemen, with fifty men running before him.
verses.after: Adonijah son of Haggith was exalting himself, saying, “I will be king.” He provided himself with a chariot, horsemen, and fifty men to run ahead of him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Adonijah son of Haggith exalted himself, saying, “I will be king.” He prepared for himself chariots and horsemen, with fifty men running before him.

verses.rationale: Preserves David’s failure to challenge, beauty, and birth order without making the two sons share a mother.
verses.before: His father had never troubled him by asking, “Why have you done this?” He was also very handsome, and she had borne him after Absalom.
verses.after: His father had never challenged him by asking, “Why have you done this?” He was also very handsome and had been born after Absalom.
verses.tsw_comparator: His father had never troubled him by asking, “Why have you done this?” He was also very handsome, and she had borne him after Absalom.

verses.rationale: Keeps the two supporters and their decision.
verses.before: He conferred with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, and they supported Adonijah.
verses.after: He conferred with Joab son of Zeruiah and Abiathar the priest, and they supported Adonijah.
verses.tsw_comparator: He conferred with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, and they supported Adonijah.

verses.rationale: Preserves every named nonsupporter without identifying this Shimei beyond the text.
verses.before: Yet Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and David’s warriors were not with Adonijah.
verses.after: But Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and David’s warriors did not side with Adonijah.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and David’s warriors were not with Adonijah.

verses.rationale: Keeps sacrifice, location, and the initial broad invitation before the stated exceptions.
verses.before: Adonijah sacrificed sheep, cattle, and fattened animals by the Serpent Stone, beside En-rogel. He invited all his brothers, the king’s sons, and all the men of Judah who were servants of the king.
verses.after: Adonijah sacrificed sheep, cattle, and fattened animals beside the stone of Zoheleth near En-rogel. He invited all his brothers, the king’s sons, and all the men of Judah who served the king.
verses.tsw_comparator: Adonijah sacrificed sheep, cattle, and fattened animals by the Serpent Stone, beside En-rogel. He invited all his brothers, the king’s sons, and all the men of Judah who were servants of the king.

verses.rationale: Retains every exclusion, including the explicitly named brother.
verses.before: But he did not invite Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the warriors, or his brother Solomon.
verses.after: But he did not invite Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the warriors, or his brother Solomon.
verses.tsw_comparator: But he did not invite Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the warriors, or his brother Solomon.

verses.rationale: Keeps Nathan’s urgent report and David’s lack of knowledge.
verses.before: Then Nathan said to Bathsheba, Solomon’s mother, “Have you not heard that Adonijah son of Haggith has become king, while our lord David does not know it?
verses.after: Nathan said to Bathsheba, Solomon’s mother, “Haven’t you heard that Adonijah son of Haggith has become king, while our lord David knows nothing of it?
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Nathan said to Bathsheba, Solomon’s mother, “Have you not heard that Adonijah son of Haggith has become king, while our lord David does not know it?

verses.rationale: Preserves the threatened lives as Nathan’s warning without inventing an already issued death order.
verses.before: Now come, please; let me advise you, so that you may save your life and the life of your son Solomon.
verses.after: Come, let me give you counsel so you can save your own life and the life of your son Solomon.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now come, please; let me advise you, so that you may save your life and the life of your son Solomon.

verses.rationale: Keeps the proposed speech and its appeal to an oath not previously narrated.
verses.before: Go in to King David and say to him, ‘Did you not, my lord the king, swear to your servant, saying, “Solomon your son will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne”? Why then has Adonijah become king?’
verses.after: Go in to King David and say, ‘My lord the king, did you not swear to your servant, “Your son Solomon will reign after me and sit on my throne”? Why, then, has Adonijah become king?’
verses.tsw_comparator: Go in to King David and say to him, ‘Did you not, my lord the king, swear to your servant, saying, “Solomon your son will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne”? Why then has Adonijah become king?’

verses.rationale: Retains the coordinated sequence without adding a motive beyond the plan.
verses.before: While you are still there speaking with the king, I will come in after you and confirm your words.”
verses.after: While you are still there speaking with the king, I will come in after you and confirm your words.”
verses.tsw_comparator: While you are still there speaking with the king, I will come in after you and confirm your words.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated age and attendant’s presence.
verses.before: So Bathsheba went in to the king’s chamber. The king was very old, and Abishag the Shunammite was serving the king.
verses.after: Bathsheba went to the king in his room. The king was very old, and Abishag the Shunammite was attending him.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Bathsheba went in to the king’s chamber. The king was very old, and Abishag the Shunammite was serving the king.

verses.rationale: Makes the brief courtly question natural while retaining her homage.
verses.before: Bathsheba bowed and prostrated herself before the king. The king said, “What is it you want?”
verses.after: Bathsheba bowed low before the king. He asked, “What do you need?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Bathsheba bowed and prostrated herself before the king. The king said, “What is it you want?”

verses.rationale: Preserves Bathsheba’s actual version of the reported oath, including the divine name.
verses.before: She said to him, “My lord, you swore by the LORD your God to your servant, ‘Solomon your son will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne.’
verses.after: She said, “My lord, you swore to your servant by the LORD your God, ‘Your son Solomon will reign after me and sit on my throne.’
verses.tsw_comparator: She said to him, “My lord, you swore by the LORD your God to your servant, ‘Solomon your son will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne.’

verses.rationale: Keeps the direct contrast between the rival’s action and David’s ignorance.
verses.before: But now, look: Adonijah has become king, and now, my lord the king, you do not know it.
verses.after: But now Adonijah has become king, and you, my lord the king, do not know it.
verses.tsw_comparator: But now, look: Adonijah has become king, and now, my lord the king, you do not know it.

verses.rationale: Retains her particular list rather than replacing it with Nathan’s or the narrator’s.
verses.before: He has sacrificed oxen, fattened animals, and sheep in abundance, and he has invited all the king’s sons, Abiathar the priest, and Joab commander of the army. But he has not invited Solomon your servant.
verses.after: He has sacrificed cattle, fattened animals, and sheep in great numbers. He has invited all the king’s sons, Abiathar the priest, and Joab the army commander, but he has not invited your servant Solomon.
verses.tsw_comparator: He has sacrificed oxen, fattened animals, and sheep in abundance, and he has invited all the king’s sons, Abiathar the priest, and Joab commander of the army. But he has not invited Solomon your servant.

verses.rationale: Preserves eyes and throne succession language.
verses.before: And you, my lord the king, the eyes of all Israel are upon you, waiting for you to tell them who will sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.
verses.after: My lord the king, all Israel’s eyes are on you to tell them who will sit on my lord the king’s throne after him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And you, my lord the king, the eyes of all Israel are upon you, waiting for you to tell them who will sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.

verses.rationale: Retains the ancestral death idiom and the political danger of being counted guilty.
verses.before: Otherwise, when my lord the king lies with his ancestors, I and my son Solomon will be counted as offenders.”
verses.after: Otherwise, when my lord the king lies down with his ancestors, my son Solomon and I will be treated as offenders.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Otherwise, when my lord the king lies with his ancestors, I and my son Solomon will be counted as offenders.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the exact timing that fulfills the plan.
verses.before: While she was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet came in.
verses.after: While she was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet arrived.
verses.tsw_comparator: While she was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet came in.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the entering subject and preserves full homage.
verses.before: They told the king, “Nathan the prophet is here.” He came before the king and prostrated himself before the king, with his face to the ground.
verses.after: The king was told, “Nathan the prophet is here.” Nathan entered the king’s presence and bowed facedown to the ground before him.
verses.tsw_comparator: They told the king, “Nathan the prophet is here.” He came before the king and prostrated himself before the king, with his face to the ground.

verses.rationale: Reads the contextually interrogative speech without turning it into an assertion that David authorized Adonijah.
verses.before: Nathan said, “My lord the king, have you said, ‘Adonijah will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne’?
verses.after: Nathan said, “My lord the king, did you say, ‘Adonijah will reign after me and sit on my throne’?
verses.tsw_comparator: Nathan said, “My lord the king, have you said, ‘Adonijah will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne’?

verses.rationale: Keeps Nathan’s distinct guest list and the reported acclamation.
verses.before: For today he has gone down and sacrificed oxen, fattened animals, and sheep in abundance. He has invited all the king’s sons, the commanders of the army, and Abiathar the priest. Look, they are eating and drinking before him, and they are saying, ‘May King Adonijah live!’
verses.after: Today he has gone down and sacrificed cattle, fattened animals, and sheep in great numbers. He has invited all the king’s sons, the army commanders, and Abiathar the priest. They are eating and drinking before him and saying, ‘Long live King Adonijah!’
verses.tsw_comparator: For today he has gone down and sacrificed oxen, fattened animals, and sheep in abundance. He has invited all the king’s sons, the commanders of the army, and Abiathar the priest. Look, they are eating and drinking before him, and they are saying, ‘May King Adonijah live!’

verses.rationale: Preserves all four excluded persons in Nathan’s account.
verses.before: But he did not invite me, your servant, nor Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, nor Solomon your servant.
verses.after: But he did not invite me, your servant, or Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, or your servant Solomon.
verses.tsw_comparator: But he did not invite me, your servant, nor Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, nor Solomon your servant.

verses.rationale: Follows read singular your servant rather than written plural.
verses.before: Has this thing come from my lord the king, though you have not told your servants who is to sit on the throne of my lord the king after him?”
verses.after: Has my lord the king done this without telling your servant who will sit on my lord the king’s throne after him?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Has this thing come from my lord the king, though you have not told your servants who is to sit on the throne of my lord the king after him?”

verses.rationale: Keeps the summons without inventing the timing or reason for her earlier departure.
verses.before: King David answered, “Call Bathsheba to me.” So she came before the king and stood before him.
verses.after: King David answered, “Call Bathsheba for me.” She came into the king’s presence and stood before him.
verses.tsw_comparator: King David answered, “Call Bathsheba to me.” So she came before the king and stood before him.

verses.rationale: Retains the oath’s living LORD and personal redemption history.
verses.before: The king swore and said, “As the LORD lives, who has redeemed my life from all distress,
verses.after: The king swore, “As the LORD lives, who has redeemed my life from every distress,
verses.tsw_comparator: The king swore and said, “As the LORD lives, who has redeemed my life from all distress,

verses.rationale: Keeps the emphatic today and David’s explicit confirmation of the oath.
verses.before: as I swore to you by the LORD, the God of Israel, saying, ‘Solomon your son will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne in my place,’ so I will do this today.”
verses.after: I will do today just what I swore to you by the LORD, the God of Israel: your son Solomon will reign after me and sit on my throne in my place.”
verses.tsw_comparator: as I swore to you by the LORD, the God of Israel, saying, ‘Solomon your son will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne in my place,’ so I will do this today.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the courtly forever acclamation without recasting it as a literal longevity prediction.
verses.before: Then Bathsheba bowed with her face to the ground and prostrated herself before the king. She said, “May my lord King David live forever!”
verses.after: Bathsheba bowed facedown to the ground before the king and said, “May my lord King David live forever!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Bathsheba bowed with her face to the ground and prostrated herself before the king. She said, “May my lord King David live forever!”

verses.rationale: Keeps the commissioned trio and response.
verses.before: King David said, “Call Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada to me.” So they came before the king.
verses.after: King David said, “Call Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada for me.” They came before the king.
verses.tsw_comparator: King David said, “Call Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada to me.” So they came before the king.

verses.rationale: Preserves the king’s personal mule and destination as concrete signs of authorization.
verses.before: The king said to them, “Take with you the servants of your lord. Have Solomon my son ride on my own mule, and bring him down to Gihon.
verses.after: The king told them, “Take your lord’s servants with you. Put my son Solomon on my own mule and bring him down to Gihon.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king said to them, “Take with you the servants of your lord. Have Solomon my son ride on my own mule, and bring him down to Gihon.

verses.rationale: Keeps both commissioned figures, anointing, and the prescribed acclamation.
verses.before: There Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet are to anoint him as king over Israel. Blow the ram’s horn and say, ‘May King Solomon live!’
verses.after: There Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet are to anoint him king over Israel. Blow the ram’s horn and say, ‘Long live King Solomon!’
verses.tsw_comparator: There Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet are to anoint him as king over Israel. Blow the ram’s horn and say, ‘May King Solomon live!’

verses.rationale: Retains the ascent, throne, and explicit appointment over both groups.
verses.before: Then you are to go up after him. He will come and sit on my throne, and he will reign in my place. I have appointed him to be ruler over Israel and Judah.”
verses.after: Then follow him up. He is to come and sit on my throne and reign in my place. I have appointed him ruler over Israel and Judah.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then you are to go up after him. He will come and sit on my throne, and he will reign in my place. I have appointed him to be ruler over Israel and Judah.”

verses.rationale: Keeps Amen and the wish for divine confirmation rather than declaring it already spoken.
verses.before: Benaiah son of Jehoiada answered the king, “Amen! May the LORD, the God of my lord the king, affirm it.
verses.after: Benaiah son of Jehoiada answered the king, “Amen! May the LORD, the God of my lord the king, say so too.
verses.tsw_comparator: Benaiah son of Jehoiada answered the king, “Amen! May the LORD, the God of my lord the king, affirm it.

verses.rationale: Follows read be and retains the comparative greatness as a blessing.
verses.before: As the LORD has been with my lord the king, so may he be with Solomon; and may he make his throne greater than the throne of my lord King David.”
verses.after: As the LORD has been with my lord the king, may he be with Solomon and make his throne greater than the throne of my lord King David.”
verses.tsw_comparator: As the LORD has been with my lord the king, so may he be with Solomon; and may he make his throne greater than the throne of my lord King David.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the escort and enacted instructions.
verses.before: So Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, the Cherethites, and the Pelethites went down. They set Solomon on King David’s mule and led him to Gihon.
verses.after: Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and Pelethites went down. They put Solomon on King David’s mule and brought him to Gihon.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, the Cherethites, and the Pelethites went down. They set Solomon on King David’s mule and led him to Gihon.

verses.rationale: Keeps Zadok as the actual anointer named here and distinguishes the oil horn from the signal horn.
verses.before: Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tent and anointed Solomon. Then they blew the ram’s horn, and all the people said, “May King Solomon live!”
verses.after: Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tent and anointed Solomon. They blew the ram’s horn, and all the people shouted, “Long live King Solomon!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tent and anointed Solomon. Then they blew the ram’s horn, and all the people said, “May King Solomon live!”

verses.rationale: Preserves the exuberant earth-splitting image without making a separate geological report.
verses.before: All the people went up after him, playing flutes and rejoicing with great joy, so that the earth split open with their sound.
verses.after: All the people followed him up, playing pipes and rejoicing with great joy. The earth split with the sound of them.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the people went up after him, playing flutes and rejoicing with great joy, so that the earth split open with their sound.

verses.rationale: Keeps meal timing and Joab’s recognition of the signal.
verses.before: Adonijah and all his invited guests heard it as they finished eating. Joab heard the sound of the ram’s horn and said, “Why is the sound of the city in an uproar?”
verses.after: Adonijah and all his guests heard it as they finished eating. When Joab heard the ram’s horn, he asked, “Why is the city in such an uproar?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Adonijah and all his invited guests heard it as they finished eating. Joab heard the sound of the ram’s horn and said, “Why is the sound of the city in an uproar?”

verses.rationale: Retains the mistaken good-man/good-news inference that echoes the runners in 2 Samuel.
verses.before: While he was still speaking, Jonathan son of Abiathar the priest came. Adonijah said, “Come in, for you are a worthy man, and you must bring good news.”
verses.after: While he was still speaking, Jonathan son of Abiathar the priest arrived. Adonijah said, “Come in! You are a worthy man, and you must be bringing good news.”
verses.tsw_comparator: While he was still speaking, Jonathan son of Abiathar the priest came. Adonijah said, “Come in, for you are a worthy man, and you must bring good news.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the sharp correction and David’s authorization.
verses.before: Jonathan answered Adonijah, “No! Our lord King David has made Solomon king.
verses.after: Jonathan answered Adonijah, “No. Our lord King David has made Solomon king.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jonathan answered Adonijah, “No! Our lord King David has made Solomon king.

verses.rationale: Preserves the report’s repeated escort and mule details.
verses.before: The king sent with him Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, the Cherethites, and the Pelethites; and they set him on the king’s mule.
verses.after: The king sent Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and Pelethites with him. They put him on the king’s mule.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king sent with him Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, the Cherethites, and the Pelethites; and they set him on the king’s mule.

verses.rationale: Keeps Jonathan’s joint attribution rather than harmonizing it with the narrator’s singular anointer in verse 39.
verses.before: Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet have anointed him king at Gihon. They have gone up from there rejoicing, and the city is in an uproar. That is the sound you have heard.
verses.after: Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anointed him king at Gihon. They came up from there rejoicing, and the city is in an uproar. That is the noise you heard.
verses.tsw_comparator: Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet have anointed him king at Gihon. They have gone up from there rejoicing, and the city is in an uproar. That is the sound you have heard.

verses.rationale: Preserves the additional decisive enthronement report.
verses.before: Solomon has also sat on the throne of the kingdom.
verses.after: Solomon has even taken his seat on the royal throne.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Solomon has also sat on the throne of the kingdom.

verses.rationale: Follows read God rather than your God and keeps name and throne comparisons.
verses.before: Moreover, the king’s servants came to bless our lord King David, saying, ‘May your God make Solomon’s name better than your name, and make his throne greater than your throne.’ And the king bowed himself on the bed.
verses.after: And the king’s servants came to bless our lord King David, saying, ‘May God make Solomon’s name better than your name and his throne greater than your throne.’ The king bowed on his bed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moreover, the king’s servants came to bless our lord King David, saying, ‘May your God make Solomon’s name better than your name, and make his throne greater than your throne.’ And the king bowed himself on the bed.

verses.rationale: Preserves David’s reported thanksgiving and personal witnessing.
verses.before: The king also said, ‘Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who today has given one to sit on my throne while my own eyes see it.’”
verses.after: The king also said, ‘Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who today has given someone to sit on my throne while my own eyes can see it.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: The king also said, ‘Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who today has given one to sit on my throne while my own eyes see it.’”

verses.rationale: Keeps fear and the collapse of the gathering.
verses.before: Then all Adonijah’s invited guests trembled, rose up, and each went their own way.
verses.after: All Adonijah’s guests trembled, got up, and went their separate ways.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then all Adonijah’s invited guests trembled, rose up, and each went their own way.

verses.rationale: Retains the refuge gesture without assuming it guarantees protection.
verses.before: Adonijah, fearing Solomon, rose and went away, and took hold of the horns of the altar.
verses.after: Adonijah was afraid of Solomon. He got up, went to the altar, and took hold of its horns.
verses.tsw_comparator: Adonijah, fearing Solomon, rose and went away, and took hold of the horns of the altar.

verses.rationale: Keeps the requested oath and explicit feared execution.
verses.before: It was told Solomon, “Look, Adonijah fears King Solomon. See, he has taken hold of the horns of the altar, saying, ‘Let King Solomon swear to me today that he will not put his servant to death by the sword.’”
verses.after: Solomon was told, “Adonijah is afraid of King Solomon. He has taken hold of the altar’s horns and says, ‘Let King Solomon swear to me today that he will not put his servant to death by the sword.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: It was told Solomon, “Look, Adonijah fears King Solomon. See, he has taken hold of the horns of the altar, saying, ‘Let King Solomon swear to me today that he will not put his servant to death by the sword.’”

verses.rationale: Preserves conditional clemency rather than converting it into the unconditional oath requested.
verses.before: Solomon said, “If he proves to be a worthy man, not a hair of his will fall to the ground. But if evil is found in him, he will die.”
verses.after: Solomon said, “If he proves to be a worthy man, not one hair of his head will fall to the ground. But if evil is found in him, he will die.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon said, “If he proves to be a worthy man, not a hair of his will fall to the ground. But if evil is found in him, he will die.”

verses.rationale: Clarifies the subject of the homage and keeps the brief dismissal without adding reconciliation.
verses.before: So King Solomon sent and brought him down from the altar. He came and prostrated himself before King Solomon, and Solomon said to him, “Go to your house.”
verses.after: King Solomon sent men to bring him down from the altar. Adonijah came and bowed before King Solomon, who told him, “Go home.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So King Solomon sent and brought him down from the altar. He came and prostrated himself before King Solomon, and Solomon said to him, “Go to your house.”

comparative_references.scope: All 53 TSW verses read after drafting independently from every pinned Hebrew verse and its source notes.
